cross_checks_lidar.assessment: Plausible. Photos show 4 original storeys (raised ground + 2 fin floors + terrace floor) under the deep roof slab, plus a 2-storey addition; ground-level photo proportions (66, near-frontal overcast) put the addition at ~0.6x the original block height -> original ~17.5 m, addition ~11 m (two ~5.5 m storeys incl. interstitial/mechanical), total ~28.5 m, matching the LiDAR 28.4 m eave. The 2014 addition is storeys 5 and 6 (the top two). height:max 32.6 m = ~4 m rooftop mechanical enclosures seen in the 2025 ortho and in the 2002 rooftop photo.
cross_checks_lidar.footprint: 87.0 x 46.0 m, long axis bearing 30 deg; Freret frontage is the 46 m SSW side; roof:planes=1 flat agrees with photos and ortho (roof now largely covered by PV arrays, which the ortho-derived roof colour will pick up as dark blue).
cross_checks_lidar.model_material_gap: build_model.py uses one beige WALL=[214,206,194] (#d6cec2). The real lower 17.5 m is a cooler, greyer greige precast (#c0bdb5 sunlit / #a5a097 diffuse) dominated by vertical fin shadows; the top 11 m is a distinctly different light blue-grey metal box (#b4bec6) with a black-and-white loggia on the ESE side. Recommended: split the wall material at z~17.5 m, darken/desaturate the lower wall, add fin relief or a fin-shadow texture, and a loggia texture on the ESE face.

notes: Addition layout was contradictory from ground photos alone (24/54/55 vs 64/66); the 2025 rotated ortho settles it: the loggia 'teeth' run the full ESE edge only; the other three edges are plain. Photo 43's Commons GPS (NE of the building) is consistent with this; a sun-angle argument that it was the Freret face was wrong.
Concrete-building photos at Freret/McAlister (Stern Hall) look superficially similar (pilotis, precast) and were excluded after inspection.

Transient conditions in the set: 2013 silver ducts on piers (renovation), Nov 2021 sidewalk scaffold canopy and tan boarding on Freret ground floor, 2019 'Commons' construction fence along Newcomb Place.

Colour caveats: 2007/2013/2026 sunlit samples carry warm sun + blue sky-fill; 64 (2019, even light) is the best neutral reference for the precast; the sunlit aluminium panels of the addition reflect sky (#c0d3e9) and look much bluer than their diffuse colour (#b4bec6).
